entries.subject: DAMIT 444: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-444.txt. Model 444, version 2012-07-30, pole (98°, -60°), period 12.79953 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Marciniak et al. (2012), Photometry and models of selected main belt asteroids IX. Introducing Interactive Service for Asteroid Models (ISAM)
entries.finding: [Marciniak et al. (2012), Photometry and models of selected main belt asteroids IX. Introducing Interactive Service for Asteroid Models (ISAM)](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012A%26A...545A.131M) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI AcuA
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — included as an explicitly approximate thermal size transfer. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 114.19 ± 1.52 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 127 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 445, pole ['261', '-70'], [Model 445](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/445) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 445: pole (261°, -70°), 12.79954 h, version 2012-07-30. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
